full_judgment: 15. From a perusal of the Agreement for Sale of 1976 and the decrees passed in Title Suit No. 83 of 1977 and 1019 of 1981 nowhere is it found that the possession was delivered to the Petitioner by Md. Ishaque or he got the possession through Court. The preamble of the Gazette published on 23.9.86 shows that the declaration by its own express terms permits of construction to the effect that the properties listed in the Notification have already been taken control of by the Government and that the Notification is predicated on that essential fact of control assumed over such property . Furthermore, this has to be read with Section 114, illustration (e) of the Evidence Act, 1872 that permits of a presumption of regularity to be attached to all governmental function discharged in due course. Furthermore, the Petitioner could not satisfy the Court of Settlement by producing any evidence that the vendor Md. Ishaque was in possession of the property in question at the time of execution of the alleged bainanama in the year 1976 or indeed before or after the P.O. 16 of 1972 came into force. From this it is to be deduced that the Notification as above records not only the listing of certain properties as abandoned properties but more importantly the fact of these having passed into the control, supervision and management of the Government at the material date in due course.
